description: One planted block inside a parcel: what grows on it, when it went in, what condition it is in, and the food-safety facts a Produce Safety Rule inspector asks about that ground. The unit is the block a crew is sent to and a spray is recorded against, which is the same unit a cost centre allocates to.

fields.description: What the block is called on the radio: 'Yellow Camp Block 3', 'North 40'. The docname is built from this and the parcel's abbreviation, so two parcels may each have a 'Block 3'.
fields.label: Field Name

fields.description: The parcel this block is part of. A field cannot move between parcels: ground does not move, and a block that turns out to be on the neighbouring parcel was mis-registered rather than relocated.
fields.label: Parcel

fields.description: The company whose books carry the parcel. Copied from the parcel rather than set here, because a field on Highland's ground belongs to Highland whatever anyone types.
fields.label: Owning Entity

fields.description: Planted acres in this block. The sum of a parcel's fields cannot exceed the parcel's own acreage — roads, ditches and headlands mean it usually should not come close.
fields.label: Acreage

fields.description: The block number as the crew and the old records know it. Free text, because legacy block ids are not numbers ('3A', 'N-12').
fields.label: Block Number

fields.description:
THE BUYER'S NAME FOR THIS BLOCK, and the only identifier on this record a person outside the farm ever types. Short, stable and buyer-facing — 'YC-3' for Yellow Camp Block 3 — it goes on the purchase order, comes back on the settlement, and is how a buyer asks for the same fruit next season without knowing or caring what the docname is.

IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT `block_number`. The block number is what the crew and the old records call it, is duplicated across parcels on purpose, and changes when somebody re-splits a block. A ticker is promised to somebody outside the business, so it is unique across the company and is meant never to move. Ten characters, because it has to fit in a column on a paper settlement sheet.

EMPTY IS THE NORMAL STATE. Most blocks are never sold by name, and a farm that has not made this promise to anybody should not be made to invent one.
fields.label: Block Ticker

fields.description: The id this block carries in the Farm App, for the sync bridge to match on. Set once at import and not edited afterwards: it is somebody else's primary key.
fields.label: Farm App ID

fields.description: The Cost Center this block's costs are booked to, when it has its own. Set by link_field_to_cost_center, which checks the cost centre is on the same books and is not a group.
fields.label: Cost Center

fields.description: What grows here. Defaulted to Cherry because that is what this was built for, and left as free text because a block of table grapes is not a schema change.
fields.label: Crop

fields.description: Bing, Rainier, Sweetheart, Chelan, Skeena — or whatever is actually planted. Free text on purpose: a Select would refuse the next variety somebody puts in the ground. list_fields reports the varieties already on the site, which is the suggestion list worth having.
fields.label: Variety

fields.description: Mazzard, Gisela 6, Krymsk 5. Determines vigour and spacing, and is the first thing a consultant asks.
fields.label: Rootstock

fields.description: The year the trees went in. Age drives yield expectation, replant timing and what an appraiser calls the block.
fields.label: Planting Year

fields.description: Trees per acre. With acreage this gives the tree count, which is the denominator for per-tree cost and for a replant estimate.
fields.label: Planting Density (per acre)

fields.description: Which of this block's crop's own catalogue varieties (`Crop.varieties`) are actually planted here, and what share of the block each covers — the Pearl blocks carry Black Pearl, Burgundy Pearl and Ebony Pearl in one field, which the single `variety` column above can only ever name one of. A LINK, NOT A SECOND CATALOGUE: rootstock, pollination group, yield and Brix stay on `Crop Variety` and are never copied here. `variety`, `rootstock`, `planting_year` and `planting_density_per_acre` above remain the PRIMARY/LEGACY answer for a single-variety block and are never derived from this table or written back to it.
fields.label: Varieties

fields.description: How the block is doing. Fallow is a condition, not a crop: a block out of production still has acreage, a cost centre and a water right.
fields.label: Condition

fields.description:
Which Soil Compaction Profile this block's ground follows — the two hour figures the irrigation/compaction overlay reads to decide whether a tractor may go on it after a set. OPTIONAL, AND AN EMPTY ONE IS NOT A GUESS: a block naming no profile falls back to the shipped 24/48-hour default and the overlay reports `thresholds_source` as `default` rather than presenting the fallback as this farm's own measurement.

IT IS ON THE BLOCK AND NOT ON THE ZONE. The soil belongs to the ground; an irrigation zone is a way of watering some of it, and resolves its profile through the block it names.
fields.label: Soil Compaction Profile

fields.description: The first day this block was productive in its current planting cycle — past the pre-yield years for a perennial. THE DENOMINATOR OF EVERY PER-ACRE METRIC IS WHAT IS PRODUCTIVE, NOT WHAT IS OWNED: a block still coming into bearing has acreage, a cost centre and a water right and earns nothing, and counting it flatters nothing while understating every per-acre figure the operation is judged on. Empty means unknown rather than zero, and a block with no date is EXCLUDED from the denominator with a warning rather than assumed productive — see get_sustainable_cf_per_acre.
fields.label: Productive From

fields.description: The last day it was productive, if it has been pulled, retired or put back into transition. NULL MEANS STILL PRODUCTIVE, which is the ordinary case and is why this is not defaulted — a date here stops the acreage counting from it, pro-rated, so a block pulled in July earns for half the year rather than for none of it or all of it.
fields.label: Productive Through

fields.description: When a perennial stops being capital under construction and becomes a crop — commonly year three or four for cherry, and it varies by variety and rootstock. Kept separate from Productive From so a block still inside its pre-yield years is COUNTED AND REPORTED rather than merely absent: those acres are next year's denominator, and a reader who cannot see them coming cannot read the trend.
fields.label: Pre-Yield End

fields.description: Food safety and worker protection facts about this ground. They are here rather than in a compliance register because they are the same facts the operation runs on: 'when was this block last sprayed' is a re-entry-interval question before it is a WPS report, and a block with no hygiene station is a block a crew cannot legally be sent to.
fields.label: Food Safety and Worker Protection

fields.description: The last application recorded on this block. Answers the re-entry interval question for a crew waiting at the gate, and is the per-field line of a WPS record-keeping report. Where farm_precision_ag is installed the read tools take the later of this and the newest Spray Log, and say which they used.
fields.label: Last Spray Date

fields.description: When the agricultural water serving this block was last tested. FSMA Produce Safety Rule Subpart E. Per-zone tests live on the Irrigation Zone; this is the block-level answer where the water is not zoned.
fields.label: Water Test Last Date

fields.description: The last recorded sign of animal intrusion — droppings, tracks, damage. FSMA Subpart I requires the assessment before harvest, and the answer decides whether fruit off this block can be picked at all.
fields.label: Wildlife Intrusion Last Report

fields.description: Ticked when this block grows produce that is eaten raw and is therefore inside the Produce Safety Rule's covered-produce scope. It changes what the other fields on this section mean, which is why it is a field and not a note.
fields.label: Food Safety Zone

fields.description: Ticked when toilets and handwashing are available within a quarter mile of this block, as FSMA Subpart L and the WPS both require before a crew works it.
fields.label: Worker Hygiene Station Present

fields.description: Certification attaches to GROUND, not to a commodity. A crop-level organic flag cannot answer 'how many acres are certified' on a farm running Gala on eight certified blocks and twelve conventional ones — there is one Crop record and one boolean, and the honest answer is unobtainable from it. This is the per-block state, and it is where the acreage sum comes from.
fields.label: Organic Certification

fields.description: Where this block stands. A SELECT RATHER THAN A CHECKBOX BECAUSE THE THREE YEARS OF TRANSITION ARE THE PART A BUYER AND AN INSPECTOR BOTH ASK ABOUT, and a checkbox records the end state and loses them. Left empty on purpose for a block nobody has answered for: blank means unasked, which is a different fact from Conventional, and defaulting would turn every unanswered block into a stated one.
fields.label: Organic Status

fields.description: Computed from Organic Status on every save and NOT editable — a derived flag a person can set independently is a flag that will disagree with the status it came from, and the one that is wrong is always the one nobody edited. It exists so 'SUM(acreage) WHERE organic_certified' is one filter rather than a string comparison, and so a caller that only wants the boolean does not have to know the vocabulary.
fields.label: Organic Certified

fields.description: Who certified it: Oregon Tilth, CCOF, WSDA. Free text, because the accreditied certifier list changes and a Select would have to be migrated when it does. An agency recorded on a block whose status is Conventional is a contradiction, and the field tools say so rather than refusing it — a block mid-application really does have an agency and no certificate yet.
fields.label: Organic Certifying Agency

fields.description: When the transition began. The National Organic Program requires thirty-six months from the last prohibited application before ground can be certified, so this date is what says when the block becomes eligible — and it stays worth keeping after certification, because it is the evidence for the window that was served.
fields.label: Transition Start Date

fields.description: The FSA farm number this block is administered under. One farm number covers several tracts, and several parcels. Written by import_fsa_clu_boundaries from the county office's own CLU file; it is what an acreage report, an ARC/PLC election and a crop insurance schedule are all filed against.
fields.label: FSA Farm Number

fields.description: The FSA tract number. A tract is a unit of ownership history rather than a tax lot, so one Parcel may hold several tracts and one tract may cross two parcels. This is half of the pair the office says out loud — 'tract 1234, field 3' — and half of what a re-import matches on.
fields.label: FSA Tract Number

fields.description: The CLU (field) number within the tract. The other half of 'tract 1234, field 3'.
fields.label: FSA Field Number

fields.description: FSA's own identifier for this Common Land Unit, which is a GUID. NOT UNIQUE HERE ON PURPOSE: a farm that splits one CLU into two blocks it manages differently is a normal thing to do, and both blocks then carry the same CLU identifier honestly. It is the first thing a re-import matches on, which is what makes next year's file an update rather than a second copy of the farm.
fields.label: CLU Identifier

fields.description: FSA's calculated acreage for this CLU, kept exactly as the file gave it. This is the number a payment is made on, so it is worth having beside the app's own — but nothing here computes with it: Computed Area (acres) comes from the polygon and is what a per-acre figure uses.
fields.label: FSA Calculated Acres

fields.description: FSA's highly erodible land classification for this CLU — typically HEL, NHEL, UHEL or EX. Conservation compliance on a HEL field is a condition of every program payment the farm receives.
fields.label: HEL Classification

fields.description: When this block last took a boundary from an FSA CLU file. FSA revises CLUs — a split, a combination, a re-measure — so a boundary imported three years ago may no longer be the one the acreage report is measured against.
fields.label: CLU Imported On

fields.description: The shape on the ground. Everything below the polygon is DERIVED from it on save and must not be edited by hand — a figure a person can change independently of the polygon is a figure that will disagree with it, and the disagreement surfaces as a geofence saying no to somebody standing in the right place.
fields.label: Boundary

fields.description: The block boundary as a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, in [longitude, latitude] degrees. Set it with the boundary tool rather than by hand: they validate the shape and recompute everything derived from it. Zones on this block are expected to sit inside it; one that does not is reported rather than refused, because a shared water line really can cross a boundary.
fields.label: Boundary (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. Where a map opens, and the cheap first cut for a distance query. For a shape whose true centroid falls outside it — a block wrapped round a farmstead — this is an interior point instead, because centring on the farmstead is centring on somebody else's ground.
fields.label: Centroid Latitude

fields.description: Computed. See Centroid Latitude.
fields.label: Centroid Longitude

fields.description: Computed. A bounding box is a guaranteed superset of the shape it bounds, which is what makes it the only safe cheap prefilter for 'is this point inside' — a candidate set built from it can never miss the right answer.
fields.label: Bounding Box (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. JSON of {resolution: [cells]} at resolutions 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, holding every cell the shape TOUCHES. Not every cell whose centre is inside it: an orchard block is smaller than one cell at resolutions 6 to 8, so a centre-based fill returns nothing for most fields and an index built on it would answer 'in no field' for a point plainly in one.
fields.label: H3 Cells

fields.description: Computed from the polygon by spherical excess. This is a different number from the acreage somebody typed and both are worth having: a deed, a GIS trace and a tape measure routinely disagree by a few percent. A gap over 5% is reported; over 25% the boundary is refused, because at that point one of the two figures is about a different piece of ground.
fields.label: Computed Area (acres)

fields.description: Where this block's imagery comes from and what the last pull said. Imagery is per-field rather than per-zone: a satellite does not resolve a valve.
fields.label: Satellite Imagery

fields.description: Sentinel-2, Planet Labs, Landsat, or whoever else. Free text, because the provider a farm can afford changes and a Select would have to be migrated when it does.
fields.label: Satellite Provider

fields.description: The provider's own handle on the scene: a Sentinel scene id, a tile URL, a capture timestamp. Free text because every provider names its assets differently and none of them will agree to ours.
fields.label: Imagery Asset Reference

fields.description: When imagery for this block was last processed. What decides whether the next pull is due is this date AND the crop cycle AND whether a boundary exists at all — not a calendar tick on its own.
fields.label: Last NDVI Pull

fields.description: Mean NDVI over the block at the last pull. The index runs -1 to 1, not 0 to 1: water and bare soil read negative, and clamping the floor to zero would make a flooded block indistinguishable from an unmeasured one.
fields.label: Last NDVI Mean

fields.description: Spread of NDVI across the block. The mean says how the block is doing; this says whether it is doing it evenly, which is the number that finds a failed irrigation set.
fields.label: Last NDVI Std Dev

name: Field
